title: Fourier coefficient under single-coordinate noise
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite set with probability law $\pi$, and let $\iota$ be a finite nonempty index set. Suppose $\Omega$ has a real orthonormal basis indexed by $\iota$ under $\pi$, with one basis vector equal to the constant function $1$. For any coordinate $i$ among the $n$ coordinates, any real $\rho$, any function $f:(\Omega^n)\to\mathbb R$, and any multi-index $a\in\iota^n$, the Fourier coefficient of the single-coordinate noise operator applied to $f$ at $a$ is the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $a$ multiplied by $1$ if $a_i$ is the constant index, and by $\rho$ otherwise.
hypotheses_covered: $\pi$ is a probability mass function on $\Omega$
$\iota$ is finite, nonempty, and has decidable equality
The basis is indexed by $\iota$ and spans the real-valued functions on $\Omega$
The basis vector at the distinguished index is constant $1$
$i$ is a coordinate among the $n$ coordinates
